member.name: M:GrpcLibrary.CalibrationProcessor.CalibrateByPerson
member.summary: Works out the camera positions from a person standing in front of the column. The person stands straight at the normal photo distance, looks ahead and holds still; the server scans the column three times (about ten seconds) and orders the cameras by where each one sees the face. The result is a PROPOSAL: nothing is stored until it is sent with (see PersonCalibrationResult.ToCalibration()). When the answer is not unambiguous (a camera did not see the face, two cameras too close to tell apart, the person moved) success is false and message says what to change. Needs server 1.1.15 / image 2.0.14 or later; an older server answers UNIMPLEMENTED.
member.returns: The proposed position per attached camera.

member.name: M:GrpcLibrary.CalibrationProcessor.CalibrateBySurroundings
member.summary: Works out the camera positions from what the cameras see, with NOBODY in front of the column: the server grabs a frame from every camera, measures the vertical shift between neighbouring cameras' views, twice, and orders the cameras by the fitted offset (the lowest camera is position 1). It needs a scene with detail; on a plain backdrop, with two cameras at the same height or when the two rounds disagree, success is false and message says why (followed by "Use 'By a person' instead."). The result is a PROPOSAL, like : nothing is stored until it is sent with (see SurroundingsCalibrationResult.ToCalibration()). It takes about 8-22 s for six cameras and is refused (RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED) while a capture runs. Needs server 1.1.25 or newer (Server 2.0: the matching image); an older server answers UNIMPLEMENTED. Added in 1.5.5.
member.returns: The proposed position and the fitted vertical offset per attached camera.

member.summary: Owns the GrpcChannel shared by the processors. The channel can be swapped at runtime with SetAddress, so an IP-address change takes effect immediately without restarting the application. gRPC clients are cheap wrappers, so processors create a fresh client per call.
member.remarks:
Which server a processor talks to:
Constructed without an address (or with the default "http://localhost:50051"): the shared channel, i.e. .
Constructed with another address: that address, so one application can talk to several kiosks with one processor per kiosk (the 1.4 behaviour).

Constructing a processor never changes the shared address.

A Set call of one of these settings changes the value in force; by default the server also saves it on the column about 2 s later, and with GrpcChannelProvider.UseColumnSession it waits for SaveColumnStandard. member.name: M:GrpcLibrary.SettingsProcessor.SaveColumnStandard(System.String[])
member.summary: This method saves the changed column settings (no names) or the named ones as the column's standard on its LED board (the revision goes up by one; the other settings on the board stay as they are). The LED layout and geometry are always saved together. When the board is not connected (or does not take the file) the save is kept by the server and written when the same board is back (ColumnSaveOutcome.Pending). Errors: an unknown name is INVALID_ARGUMENT; a server that never saw a column is FAILED_PRECONDITION. A column whose adoption is not on its board yet (the server tries again at the next connect) refuses the save: FAILED_PRECONDITION while its board is not connected, UNAVAILABLE ("the column's LED board did not take the file") while it is. A column whose files a newer FaceSnap server wrote is left as it is: FAILED_PRECONDITION ("the column's profile was written by a newer FaceSnap server"). Requires a server with the column profile; older servers answer UNIMPLEMENTED.
member.param: Setting names (ColumnSettingNames); none = every changed one.
member.returns: Written, Pending or Nothing (nothing was changed), the names, and the profile after it.

member.name: M:GrpcLibrary.SettingsProcessor.DiscardColumnChanges(System.String[])

member.param: Setting names (ColumnSettingNames); none = every changed one.
member.returns: The profile after it.

member.name: T:GrpcLibrary.LapSubject
member.summary: Settings for one capture (spec 2026-10-11, section 3.2). Every field is optional: a field that is set overrides the kiosk's value for this capture only; an absent field means the kiosk's value in force. A value outside its rule is refused with INVALID_ARGUMENT before any light or camera is touched, and so is a field this server does not know (by field number). A manual capture uses only jpeg_quality, glare_free_light, photo_light, leds_off_for_photo and colour_correction; any other field is refused there. A child on a parent's lap (spec 2026-10-19): the subject is the LOWER face in the frame (the child), not the nearest one.
